title: Static Routing
description: Configure static routes on a router to enable connectivity between three networks. Understand how the routing table is populated and how to use the 'show ip route' command for verification.
scenario: R1 already has its interfaces configured. You need to add static routes so that traffic destined for the 172.16.0.0/24 and 172.16.1.0/24 remote networks is forwarded through the 10.0.0.2 next-hop (your ISP gateway). Also add a default route for internet-bound traffic.

tasks.description: Add a static route to 172.16.0.0/24 via next-hop 10.0.0.2
tasks.hint: In global config mode: ip route 172.16.0.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2

tasks.description: Add a static route to 172.16.1.0/24 via next-hop 10.0.0.2
tasks.hint: In global config mode: ip route 172.16.1.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2

tasks.description: Add a default route (0.0.0.0/0) via next-hop 10.0.0.2
tasks.hint: ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 10.0.0.2 — the quad-zero network and mask matches any destination
